original_target.title: Does the circle minimize the planar Euclidean photon-number integral?
original_target.area: Geometric curve functionals and mathematical physics

full_original_statement:
Let $`C`$ be any smooth, regular, simple closed curve in the Euclidean plane, parameterized by $`x:S^1\to\mathbb R^2`$. For $`t\ne s`$, put $`\Delta=x(t)-x(s)`$ and
```math
v_t^\perp=x'(t)-\frac{x'(t)\cdot\Delta}{|\Delta|^2}\Delta,
 \qquad
 v_s^\perp=x'(s)-\frac{x'(s)\cdot\Delta}{|\Delta|^2}\Delta.
```

The Euclidean photon-number integral of [1, equation (2)] is
```math
n_C=-2\int_{S^1}\!\int_{S^1}
      \frac{v_t^\perp\cdot v_s^\perp}{|x(t)-x(s)|^2}\,dt\,ds.
```

Is $`n_C\geq2\pi^2`$ for every such planar curve $`C`$? The circle has value $`2\pi^2`$ [1].

sources.scope_comparison: The actual ellipse formula is (xi+xi^−1)pi² and gives the circle minimum only within ellipses. The source retains the unrestricted planar Jordan-curve minimum as a conjecture. Its unbounded-below examples in ambient dimension greater than two cannot refute the plane-only target. Photon entropy inequalities and differently regularized Mobius knot energies are distinct functionals. Current focused searches found no matching full proof or announced settlement.
